title: DentaCare
lead: An admin panel for dental clinics — every screen of the design built end to end, in three languages, with light and dark themes.

facts.label: STATUS
facts.value: All design screens shipped, on mock data

sections.title: One place to run a clinic
paragraphs: DentaCare brings a dental clinic's daily work into one admin panel: patient records with a dental chart (odontogram), an appointment calendar, treatment plans, billing, inventory, reports, staff shifts, users and role-based access control.
I implemented every screen from the design file as a Next.js App Router app. The data layer runs on mock requests behind a single helper, so wiring up the real backend is a swap, not a rewrite.

sections.title: Feature-Sliced Design
paragraphs: The codebase follows Feature-Sliced Design. Imports only ever go downward, slices on the same layer never import each other, and every slice exposes a public API.
The rules aren't just conventions — ESLint boundaries and Steiger enforce them, and a Husky pre-commit hook rejects any commit with lint errors.

items.label: FORMS
items.title: Everything goes through React Hook Form
items.text: Create and edit forms, settings, table filters, search, sorting — all one pattern, validated with Zod schemas whose messages are translation keys.

items.label: I18N
items.title: Three languages, one key tree
items.text: next-intl with ru, ky and en. The locale lives in a cookie, not the URL; numbers, dates and money are formatted per locale with ICU placeholders.

items.label: DATA
items.title: Backend-ready mock layer
items.text: TanStack Query on top of an Axios instance. Mutations go through one mock helper that gets replaced by real API calls once the backend is connected.

items.label: RENDERING
items.title: Server Components by default
items.text: “use client” only where interactivity, browser APIs or hooks need it — plus a custom UI kit with modals, tables, toasts and confirm dialogs.
